newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat's cabinet discusses establishment of state.
newsitem.headline: Arafat's cabinet discusses establishment of state.

text.p: President Yasser Arafat on Friday led the Palestinian Authority cabinet in a discussion of the establishment of a Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital, a PLO official said.

"We discussed today the establishment of the independent Palestinian state with its capital in Jerusalem," PLO official Tayeb Abdel-Rahim told reporters after the meeting in the West Bank town of Hebron. He did not elaborate.
Since Israel's handover of 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule last Friday, Arafat, in defiance of Israel, has stepped up statements that he will declare a Palestinian state.

The PLO head said in Cairo on Wednesday: "The Palestinian state is not an Israeli issue. This is an Arab and international issue. After the interim agreements, we will declare an independent Palestinian state."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that any unilateral declaration of a Palestinian state would violate peace deals and that he had a plan ready if Arafat took such a step.

The Authority now controls most of the Gaza Strip and eight West Bank towns handed over by Israel under several agreements signed since 1993. The final status of these areas, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war, is to be determined in negotiations ending no later than May 1999.
Netanyahu opposes a Palestinian state and has said he will never cede to the Palestinians any part of Jerusalem, the eastern half of which Israel captured along with the West Bank.

Abdel-Rahim said the Authority cabinet had set up a team to negotiate outstanding interim issues with Israel such as an airport and safe passage between Gaza and the West Bank which are separated geographically by the state of Israel.
He said contacts would be made with Israel on Saturday over the negotiations.
